definitions.gloss: command, order, signal, word of command
definitions.explanation: A verbal command or signal given to a group to coordinate action. Commonly used in military drills, school assemblies, sports, and other organized group activities.

examples.japanese: 「{気|き}をつけ！」と{号令|ごうれい}がかかった。
{社長|しゃちょう}の{号令|ごうれい}のもと、{全社|ぜんしゃ}で{改革|かいかく}が{進|すす}められた。
examples.english: Reforms were carried out company-wide under the president's orders.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {号令|ごうれい}をかける (give a command)
- {号令|ごうれい}に{従|したが}う (follow a command)
- {号令|ごうれい}のもと (under the command of)
- {号令|ごうれい}{一下|いっか} (at a single command)

USAGE:
Most Japanese people associate {号令|ごうれい} with school life — the class monitor ({日直|にっちょく}) calls out commands like 「{起立|きりつ}！{礼|れい}！{着席|ちゃくせき}！」 (Stand! Bow! Sit!) at the start and end of each class. The word is also used in business to describe orders from leadership that set company-wide action in motion.
